name: Corfu
title: Corfu Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging | Ferries & Cruise Ships
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement at Corfu for Adriatic ro-pax ferries, cruise ships and coasters: car-deck, ballast tank and hull gauging during port calls.
h1: Ship Thickness Gauging at the Port of Corfu
intro: Corfu is the Ionian Sea's busiest passenger port, a gateway where Italian and Albanian ferries, cruise ships and Greek island services all meet within a short stretch of waterfront. Ships here work to published timetables and rarely stay long. That shapes the gauging: short, targeted scopes planned around a turnaround. Technicians travel from India to join the ship at Corfu, with a work list agreed beforehand with the superintendent.

highlights.h: Adriatic ferries on a fixed rotation
highlights.p: Ro-pax ships linking Corfu with Italian ports sail to a pattern. Gauging fits the layover, concentrating on vehicle decks, ramp structure and ballast tanks, with ship staff clearing decks of parked traffic.
Cruise ships call for a day and leave by evening. Work is limited to spaces the technical department can release, most often scrubber wash-water lines, sea-water pipework and a few voids.
Outside the tourist season passenger traffic thins and ferries run lighter schedules. That is the time for fuller deck and tank gauging, planned with the owner ahead of a spring docking.

port.h: Corfu's harbours on the Ionian coast
p: The main harbour at Corfu town lies on the island's east coast, facing the Albanian and Greek mainland across the Corfu Channel. A new port with ferry and cruise berths sits beside the old town, while the old harbour serves smaller craft. The channel is narrow at its northern end and wide open to the south, so the approach from the Adriatic is straightforward, but ships entering the harbour pass local ferries, yachts and fishing craft on a busy summer day.

Passenger traffic dominates. International ro-pax ferries run between Corfu and Italian ports on the Adriatic and Ionian coasts, domestic ferries link the island with Igoumenitsa, the mainland port facing it, and Greek islands, and cruise ships are scheduled in numbers during the season. Cargo is lighter: coasters bring supplies and building materials, coastal tankers supply fuel, and a few ships call with aggregate or other bulk goods. The seasonal swing is large, with the harbour crowded in summer and noticeably quiet in winter.

Corfu's weather is milder than the Aegean's, though winter storms from the south-west can shut berths for a day or two, and the swell inside the harbour matters for launch transfers. Ships seldom anchor for long, since the berths turn over quickly, but a ship waiting for a slot or for orders may anchor off the town in reasonable shelter. For gauging, the best windows are the winter lay-overs, when ro-pax ferries run reduced schedules and cruise calls fall away. A superintendent who books early can often secure a longer stay at a quiet berth, which turns a short targeted check into a full deck and tank programme.

facilities.h: Gauging at Corfu's berths and where ships dock instead
p: The island has a small shipyard and slipway for local craft, fishing boats and workboats, but no drydock for larger merchant ships or the big ferries. Work on the big ferries therefore happens at the quay: vehicle decks, ramps, side shell above the waterline, ballast tanks and, on cruise ships, the scrubber and sea-water pipework. When a hull docking is due, ships generally go to a yard in mainland Greece or across the Ionian Sea to Italy, and the Corfu readings are prepared for that docking.

Access depends on the berth. At the new port ferry berths, ships lie between rotations with vehicle decks empty for short periods, and the crew must agree release of the decks. Cruise berths are busier, with passengers embarking and shore excursions leaving, so gauging stays within the machinery and piping spaces the ship's engineers choose to open. In every case the ship's agent submits the technicians' details to the port authority and the ISPS security staff before arrival.
list: New port ferry berths: car-deck, ramp and ballast-tank gauging on Adriatic and Ionian ro-pax ships between rotations.
Cruise berths at the town: scrubber wash-water, sea-water piping and selected voids on cruise ships during the call.
Old harbour quays: shell and tank readings on small coasters, tugs and workboats that use the smaller berths.
Local slipway and small yard: hull gauging on fishing and harbour craft hauled out for survey.
Anchorage off the town: launch-served gauging on ships waiting for a berth, weather and swell permitting.
Handover to a docking yard: readings in TM plan format for the owner's chosen yard in Greece or Italy.

context.h: Ferries, passenger rules and Corfu's regulatory setting
p: Corfu is under Greek jurisdiction, with the Hellenic Coast Guard handling inspections and Paris MoU port state control applying to visiting foreign-flag ships. Ro-pax and cruise ships carry passenger-ship safety obligations that go beyond cargo ship rules, so a structural defect on a car deck or in the ballast system is a safety matter as well as a maintenance one. Coast Guard inspectors and flag state surveyors have a close view of the ferries on the Corfu run, which is a reason for owners to keep thickness records current.

Several EU rules push ferry owners to look at their steel. The Ship Recycling Regulation requires an up-to-date Inventory of Hazardous Materials, EU ETS covers passenger ships above the size threshold, and FuelEU Maritime is changing fuel choices. Older Adriatic ferries are being compared with newbuild alternatives, and thickness readings help an owner judge how many seasons remain in the hull. Cruise ships fitted with scrubbers have an added reason to measure wash-water pipework, because local discharge rules in the Ionian are applied through the port authority.

jobs.p: Corfu jobs are short, selective and tied to a timetable. The superintendent sends the ferry's schedule, the class survey status and the areas of concern, and the team plans the work around the turnaround. Results are returned quickly so that the owner can decide whether a repair can wait for winter or must be brought forward. Typical requests are:
list: An Adriatic ro-pax ferry between rotations: vehicle-deck plating, ramp structure and ballast-tank readings, with magnetic particle testing at ramp hinges.
A cruise ship in port for a day: wall-thickness readings on scrubber wash-water and overboard lines, taken with the system shut down.
A domestic ferry in winter lay-over: fuller gauging of decks, side shell and tanks ahead of a spring docking at a mainland yard.
A small coaster at the old harbour: hold and deck gauging after discharge, for the owner's survey preparation.
A pre-purchase check on a ferry or coaster, completed alongside before the buyer decides.

logistics: Corfu has its own international airport, with seasonal direct flights from several European cities and connections through Athens, so the team can usually reach the island without a long road transfer. Technicians from India need a Schengen visa for Greece. Because ferry and cruise timetables are fixed, mobilisation is tied to a confirmed berth and turnaround, and the agent files port access and security details with the harbour authority beforehand.

faqs.q: Can a ro-pax ferry be gauged during a short turnaround at Corfu?
faqs.a: Yes, if the scope is focused. With the vehicle deck cleared and tanks prepared, the team can cover a defined list of areas, usually ramps, deck plating near the stern and a few ballast tanks. We agree the order of priority beforehand so the most important readings are done first.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Corfu for larger ships?
faqs.a: Not for merchant ships or large ferries. The island's small yard serves local craft. Larger vessels dock on the Greek mainland or at an Italian yard, and the Corfu gauging is arranged as preparation, with readings recorded in a format the docking yard can use.

faqs.q: Can cruise ship scrubber piping be inspected while passengers are aboard?
faqs.a: Often, yes, because the piping sits in machinery spaces and tunnels away from guests. The ship's engineers shut down and isolate the system, provide access and arrange hot-work and enclosed-space permits where needed. We measure wall thickness at bends, flanges and overboard connections.

faqs.q: What is the best season for longer gauging at Corfu?
faqs.a: Winter, when passenger traffic eases and ferries run lighter timetables. Some ships lie for longer between rotations, and cruise calls are rare. That lets us plan fuller scopes on decks and tanks, although the weather can delay launch transfers at the anchorage on stormy days.
